accessibility: Accessibility is an experimental CDP domain depending on DOM.
AXNode exposes semantic role, accessible name, description, value, widget/state properties, parent/child IDs, backendDOMNodeId and frameId.
getFullAXTree accepts optional depth and frameId; getPartialAXTree and queryAXTree permit narrower retrieval.
Accessibility.enable makes AXNodeIds stable across calls but the protocol explicitly warns that enabling accessibility can impact performance until disabled.
domsnapshot: DOMSnapshot is an experimental CDP domain depending on CSS, DOM, DOMDebugger and Page.
captureSnapshot returns a flattened full DOM snapshot plus layout and optional computed-style/paint/rectangle information.
DOMSnapshot carries DOM attributes, input/check/select state, backendNodeId, frame identity, layout bounds/text and optional clickability/style detail.
The source surface is semantically richer for exact layout/DOM inspection than AX, but E1 source shape alone is not a runtime cost measurement.

comparison.AX_strength: compact interaction/meaning-oriented structure: roles, names, values, focusability/widget state and DOM/frame linkage, with bounded-depth/partial/query APIs
comparison.AX_limit: does not by itself expose the full DOM/layout/computed-style surface needed for exact spatial or markup reasoning
comparison.DOMSnapshot_strength: high-fidelity document/layout/style structure and DOM attributes
comparison.DOMSnapshot_limit: full-document snapshot semantics and broader protocol dependencies make it a plausible heavier path, but no latency/bytes/CPU claim is granted without target-browser measurement

source_level_hypothesis: For F2 browser/structural perception, an AX-first semantic structural path with on-demand DOMSnapshot escalation may preserve agent-relevant interaction semantics while avoiding unconditional full-document/layout snapshots. This is a source-derived architecture hypothesis only.
counterhypotheses: AX may omit non-accessible or visually relevant DOM structure needed by F2, forcing DOMSnapshot often enough that two-tier routing adds complexity without savings.
Persistent AX enablement may itself carry material browser overhead; stateless/bounded AX calls need measurement before promotion.
DOMSnapshot's shared string tables/columnar encoding may make its practical payload/cost more competitive than source breadth suggests.
A direct DOM/AX mixed query strategy may outperform both full AX and full DOMSnapshot for interaction tasks.
next_discriminator: Acquire E2_ARCHITECTURE_MAPPED and map AX-first/on-demand-DOMSnapshot against F2 browser/structural source semantics, promotion policy, provenance and temporal/generation boundaries. Do not claim efficiency until exact-browser payload/latency/CPU measurements exist.
